title: 2019_PMC6898916_The_maternal_antibody_against_diphtheria_tetanus_and_pertussis_s
ehr_evidence: A routinely peripheral blood sample was obtained at admission. All serum samples were frozen at − 20 °C until analysis. Anti-Dtx, anti-Ttx and anti-pertussis toxin (Ptx) IgG levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay using commercial ELISA kits (Euroimmun, Lübeck, Germany).
summary: A comparative cross-sectional study of DTP-associated maternal antibodies in 438 neonates (1-28 days) from two Chinese hospitals (Shunyi, Beijing and Qianjiang, Chongqing) showing significant regional differences in protective antibody levels.
key_findings: Mean anti-Dtx IgG was significantly lower in Qianjiang (0.04 IU/ml) than Shunyi (0.12 IU/ml), P < 0.0001.
Mean anti-Ttx IgG was significantly lower in Qianjiang (0.07 IU/ml) than Shunyi (0.18 IU/ml), P < 0.0001.
Protective anti-Dtx IgG prevalence was lower in Qianjiang (7.1%) than Shunyi (30.5%), χ2 = 21.788, P < 0.0001.
Protective anti-Ttx IgG prevalence was lower in Qianjiang (7.6%) than Shunyi (38.5%), χ2 = 33.569, P < 0.0001.
The detectable rate of anti-Ptx IgG was significantly higher in Qianjiang (39.9%) than Shunyi (30.5%).
No significant difference in protective anti-Ptx IgG rate was observed between Shunyi and Qianjiang (χ2 = 0.837, P < 0.3601).
population: 438 neonates (1-28 days old) hospitalized in Shunyi Women and Children's Hospital (Beijing) and Qianjiang Central Hospital (Chongqing)
exposure_domain: Vaccination (DTP vaccine) and maternal passive antibody transfer / regional immunization coverage
limitations: Sample size limited and all subjects collected from only two hospitals.
Vaccination status of neonates' mothers could not be obtained.
No maternal blood samples were collected for comparison.
